## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`reviewed_batch` is correct, and its tests cover the empty, all-true and mixed cases. One regression needs fixing first: the rewrite of `requirement_proven` drops the empty-list guard, so a requirement with no criteria now counts as proven.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — The old code was `bool(criteria) and all(...)`, which returned `False` for `criteria=[]`. The new `sum(...) == len(criteria)` computes `0 == 0` for `[]` and returns `True`. The new test at tests/test_proof.py:7-8 only passes non-empty lists, so it doesn't catch this. Could you put back the `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` form, or add an explicit empty check, and add an `assert not requirement_proven([])` case? — Any requirement with no attached criteria is now reported as proven, which is the opposite of what the previous code returned and the reverse of what "proof status" should mean.
